title: Swiipt Product AI-QA Result
description: Structured output contract for the canonical Product-level INDEPENDENT AI-QA review (gate g7). This is the machine-readable form of the reviewer output already defined by standards/qa-standard.md sections 3-5 and consumed by schemas/product.schema.json (qa.ai_tests). It is deliberately NOT a second QA framework and NOT a parallel QA store: the harness projects the AI-owned rows into the EXISTING product.qa.ai_tests contract and the existing harness/product-qa-gate-runner.mjs recomputes g7. Acceptance Tests and Publishing Gates remain authoritative.

review_type.description: Discriminator. The canonical Product acceptance reviewer.

overall_status.description: Reviewer verdict (qa-standard section 5). PASS requires every test to pass.

tests.description: The AI-owned Product acceptance tests only (A-J, M, N, Q, R). Evidence (K), clinical/safety (L), human journey (O) and deterministic ecosystem (P) results are NOT returned here - see authority_flags.

status.description: PASS | FAIL | REVISION_REQUIRED are the canonical ledger statuses. SOURCE_REQUIRED and HUMAN_REVIEW are honest non-PASS states that the harness records explicitly and never converts into PASS.

finding.description: What was observed, in terms of the supplied canonical material only.

evidence_location.description: Where in the supplied material the observation is anchored (field path, asset id, content section). Empty string when the test passes without a specific anchor.

recommended_action.description: Required correction when the status is not PASS. Empty string when passing.

authority_flags.description: Concerns the reviewer is NOT authorised to decide, surfaced for the owning authority (evidence/clinical/human/deterministic). The reviewer never returns a PASS for these tests and never substitutes for the owning gate. Items are advisory notes to another authority, so extra descriptive keys are tolerated; the four required keys are enforced.

scope_drift.description: qa-standard section 5: did the product change its situation definition while keeping its name (test R).

missing_information.description: Information the reviewer needed and could not find in the supplied canonical material. The reviewer must never invent it.
